findings.title: Audit evidence content is accepted without schema validation
findings.context: The binding routine hashes and parses the snapshot but checks only auditRunId and repository.head; it never validates schemas/audit-evidence.schema.json or material provenance fields.
findings.riskExplanation: A locally authored snapshot can retain the expected run ID and revision while omitting or fabricating material provenance.
findings.rootCause: Evidence binding was implemented as digest and identity checks without invoking the evidence schema.

resolution.recommended: Validate the snapshot against its schema and enforce required semantics; add malformed correctly-hashed fixtures.
tradeoffs: The artifact contract and fixtures must be versioned together to preserve historical readability.
resolution.rollout: Add failing fixtures first, update schemas and validators, then regenerate shipped project templates.
resolution.rollback: Restore the prior schema and validator together if compatibility validation fails.

verification: A correctly hashed malformed snapshot is rejected.
findings.containment: Treat affected audit records as local assessment evidence, not independently tamper-evident proof, until remediation validates.
findings.decisionRationale: Confirmed by inspection of the controlling schema and validator path; the current focused tests do not exercise this adversarial case.

findings.title: Audit validators follow report paths without canonical containment checks
findings.context: Findings evidence and schema 2.1 sourceReview paths are resolved and read without a required root, canonical containment, regular-file, or symlink check.
findings.riskExplanation: A crafted workspace can make validation consume bytes outside the repository or through redirected report paths.
findings.rootCause: The newer execution validator received canonical boundary controls, but findings and plan validation retained direct path.resolve reads.

resolution.recommended: Require repository root, canonicalize paths, reject symlinks and non-files, and reuse containedPath.

findings.title: Verification record digests are not bound to named artifacts
findings.context: Schema 2.2 requires evidenceSha256 but no evidence path, while semantic validation checks only that the digest string exists.
findings.riskExplanation: A report can claim successful provenance using any syntactically valid digest.
findings.rootCause: Verification records model a digest as metadata rather than a reference to verifiable artifact bytes.

resolution.recommended: Add content-addressed evidence references and validate containment, bytes, digest, identity, and scope.
tradeoffs: The artifact contract and fixtures must be versioned together to preserve historical readability.

findings.title: Digest equality contradicts the schema's case-insensitive format
findings.context: Schemas allow uppercase hexadecimal while the validator compares the reference, filename, and computed lowercase digest case-sensitively.
findings.riskExplanation: A schema-valid uppercase digest can be rejected, causing contract inconsistency and false failures.
findings.rootCause: Schema patterns permit mixed-case hexadecimal while semantic validation assumes lowercase writer output.

resolution.recommended: Require lowercase in schemas and writers, or normalize all digest comparisons; add uppercase fixtures.
tradeoffs: The artifact contract and fixtures must be versioned together to preserve historical readability.
resolution.rollout: Add failing fixtures first, update schemas and validators, then regenerate shipped project templates.
